Research profile

Research and supervision

Biometrics, computer vision, AI fairness, transport and infrastructure.

Master of Computing thesis, 2021

Vein Pattern Visualisation and Identification using Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks

An ethics-approved study of RGB to near-infrared vein visualisation using conditional GANs and data collected with ESR support.

Dataset: 301 participants and 602 paired RGB and near-infrared samples Supervision: Hamid Sharifzadeh and Soheil Varastehpour Recognition: Recognised by Unitec among outstanding postgraduate researchers in 2022

Class structure

How we work in class

Each session combines explanation, coding, short tasks and project work.

Step 1: Presentation

Learn the idea and why it is useful.

The presentation introduces the theory, assumptions, mathematics and examples needed for the coding work.

The explanation and practice belong together.
Git repository

Use one course repository

Clone it once. Pull updates before class. Open the project in VS Code.

Public course repository

ml-course-unitec

github.com/alikeivanmarz/ml-course-unitec
  • Course_Sessionsnotebooks, demonstrations and class tools
  • Datasetsdata used in examples and activities
  • Assignmentsassessment templates when released
  • Environment_Setupthe mlcourse environment file
  • GuidesGit, VS Code and workflow help
Step 1

Get current files

Run this before each class from the repository folder.

git pull origin main
Step 2

Activate the environment

Use the same tested Python environment for course code.

conda activate mlcourse
Step 3

Open VS Code

Open the whole repository so notebooks, data and paths remain connected.

code .
Step 4

Keep your work separate

Use your own named copies for personal and assessed work. Do not push to the instructor repository.
